input.question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?
input.ground_truth: Banks are tightly regulated by the government, required to follow thousands of laws and rules, and subject to constant inspection and detailed audits at any time. Therefore they are trusted to manage certain financial tasks.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine money is like a toy. Normally, you have a toy in your hand and you can play with it. But now, instead of holding the toy, you can keep a picture or a note that says, “I have this toy,” and everyone agrees that this note is just as good as having the toy.

Now, banks are like a big, safe toy box that everyone trusts. Only the toy box (the bank) is allowed to say, “This picture is real,” because they have special rules and grown-ups (called regulators) who check to make sure the bank is being honest. If the bank says you have a toy, other people believe them because they know the bank is careful and follows the rules.

If you tried to make your own “toy box” and say you have toys that you don’t really have, other people might not trust you. They might think you’re lying or making up toys that don’t exist. That could make people mad or confused.

So, banks are special because everyone agrees to trust them to keep track of the pretend money (electronic money), and they have to follow strict rules to make sure everything is fair and safe. That’s why you can’t just open your own “bank” and say you have lots of money—you have to prove you’re being honest and follow the rules, just like the big banks do.
